changesets.headline: One tracker for a held finger across a group of targets (an alert's or an action sheet's actions, a menu's rows, a segmented control's segments, a page control's dots): it reads the targets' rects once, resolves the finger against them (or by the owner's rule), paints or reports the highlight, and runs the target through its own click at the lift. Nothing a consumer sees changes.

`useAnimatedLayout({containerRef})` returns a handle that Collapsible and TreeList take as their new `animatedLayout` prop (`spec:AST-105`). When one of them opens or closes, the content around it inside that container (after it, and before it where the layout centers or end-aligns it) glides to its new place instead of jumping, the revealed content reveals, closing content conceals before it hides, and the chevron turns, all on one shared motion, under every pointer, a mouse included. Fixed and stuck sticky elements stay put, the glide never scrolls the container, and under Reduce Motion the change cross-fades on touch and happens at once with a mouse. A single-mode CollapsibleGroup glides every item it changes. Without the prop, nothing changes.

With an `animatedLayout` handle, content before a Collapsible or TreeList change glides too where the layout moves it: an item before the change in a centered, end-aligned or space-between row, a sibling `order` places after it, and the card around a change in a centered column. Inside a positioned, stuck sticky or top-layer ancestor of the change, only the content after the change moves: that ancestor, the wrappers inside it and the content before the change take their final place at once.
With an `animatedLayout` handle, a Collapsible or TreeList change in a long list reads every row's place before any glide starts, so the page is laid out once rather than once per gliding row.

With an `animatedLayout` handle, content after a change now glides even when it keeps a transform that leaves it in place. A resting Button (`scale(1)`, computed as `matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)`), a pressed one (`scale(0.98)`) and a row with swipe actions at rest (`translate3d(0, 0, 0)`) used to jump to their new place as if the app were moving them, and a pressed button jumped onto the button gliding beside it. A row a swipe holds open, or anything the app translates or rotates, is still left to the app.

The animated-layout module gains its internal in-place swap: old content held as one inert, transient copy while new content enters in its place, on the shared motion. Nothing uses it yet and nothing public changes. In right-to-left containers, content after a Collapsible or TreeList size change (with an `animatedLayout` handle) now glides by its inline-start edge instead of jumping.

Internal: the one module for size-change glides (`spec:AST-105`, `architecture:react-component-runtime` INV12). After a reported size change, the content after it inside a container glides to its new place on one shared internal motion role, and the changed element enters or exits on the same motion. Not exported; no component uses it yet. The public `useAnimatedLayout` hook and Collapsible's and TreeList's `animatedLayout` prop arrive together in a later release.

`useAnnounce` now delivers a message by where its caller is. Inside an open Astryx modal — a Dialog, a modal BottomSheet (standalone or a switcher step), a modal Drawer, a Lightbox, MobileNav, or CommandPalette's dialog — the message reaches a persistent live region inside that dialog, which assistive technology hears while the modal is open, instead of the page-body region the modal hides; outside a modal nothing changes. Component and app code rendered inside a modal that calls `useAnnounce` is heard without any change to it. Delivery follows exposure, in top-layer order: a message sent as a switcher step hands over reaches the entering step, forward or back; a message sent as a modal BottomSheet closes, or just before an open Dialog is unmounted, waits while the leaving modal still covers the page and is delivered at its real close to whatever is exposed then — the Dialog it was opened over, or the page body — instead of being lost; a message a modal receives while a later modal covers it is not written and its region is clear before it is on top again. Busy controls inside a modal announce their busy start through the same region, including inside a native modal an app renders without Astryx; messages written to one region before the first is exposed are joined, and an identical repeat in the same frame is said once. The region's internal marker is `data-astryx-modal-live-region="polite"` or `"assertive"` (the busy region's former `data-astryx-modal-busy-region` is gone). Not in this change: CommandPalette's own result-count messages, Lightbox's own position and zoom messages, and Selector's and MultiSelector's selection and result-count messages in their `bottom-sheet` presentation are sent from the component that renders each dialog, above it, and still use the page-body channel while that dialog is open; each component's own change follows. This meets the in-modal delivery requirement in spec:AST-086 (FR14).

useAnnounce: messages announced in the same frame are now joined, in order, into one announcement instead of the last one replacing the others, and an identical repeat is spoken once, so a screen reader no longer misses an earlier status such as a result count announced alongside a confirmation. An empty message still clears the region, including joined messages not yet spoken. This meets the shared-channel requirement in spec:AST-086 (FR9). Introduced in #8244; final-state evidence (#8294).

EmptyState now announces through the page's shared announcer regions, a visually hidden `role="status"` (polite) and `role="alert"` (assertive) pair that Astryx mounts once on `document.body`. In tests, a query such as `getByRole('status')` or `getByRole('alert')` can therefore match one of these regions rather than your component. Scope the query to your component with `within(container)`.

ChatComposerInput keeps focus and its Tab stop when disabled instead of moving focus to the page. Disabled editors block editing, paste/drop, trigger selection, imperative mutations, and submission while retaining their draft and accessible description.
ComplexSelector ignores value commits from an already-open popup while disabled, without changing focus or caller-owned content.

Propagate InputGroup disablement to compatible inputs and Button addons so child editing, opening, and form participation use their disabled behavior. Preserve nested group disablement and explicitly disabled children without modifying caller-rendered controls.

Tokenizer blocks token additions, creation, removal, and supplied removal callbacks while disabled, preserving enabled removal and focus behavior. Disabled form values are omitted instead of rendering native-disabled hidden inputs.

`astryx theme build` keeps function icon entries, so a built theme answers each `<Icon>` request with the size and variant it renders, exactly as the runtime theme does. This includes entries inherited from a built or package theme, and family builds. A built theme's `icons` field and the registry its module re-exports are React nodes, each function read at `{size: 'md'}`. A theme that lists `iconVariants` writes an `IconVariantMap` augmentation into `<theme>.variants.d.ts`, and its declaration carries the list, so a theme that extends the built theme types `variant` by those names. A function written in the theme file itself fails the build, as an inline registry always has. Themes without function entries or an icon variant list build the same output as before.

A theme icon entry in `defineTheme({icons})` or `registerIcons()` can be a pure, synchronous function of `{size, variant}`; `Icon` calls it with the size it renders at, so a theme can match its icon library's artwork or props to each Icon size. A selected function's result is final: `null` draws no glyph instead of falling back. `getIcon`, `getExtendedIcon`, `getIconRegistry`, `useIcon`, and a theme's `icons` field stay node-valued and read a function entry at `{size: 'md'}`. Existing node entries are unchanged.

A theme lists the icon variant names it supports once with `defineTheme({iconVariants})`, and reads them back from `theme.iconVariants`. A child theme that sets the list replaces the inherited one; a child that omits it inherits it. `astryx theme build` keeps the list in the built theme, so a theme extending a built theme inherits it too. Inside `defineTheme`, icon entry functions receive `variant` typed as the theme's listed names. `@astryxdesign/core/Icon` exports the augmentable `IconVariantMap` and its `IconVariant` names, which type `variant` in `registerIcons()` entries. Themes without `iconVariants` are unchanged.

`Icon` takes an optional `variant` (an `IconVariant` name) that requests the active theme's alternate artwork for a semantic icon: `<Icon icon="info" variant="filled" />`. The theme's icon entry receives the variant only when the active theme lists it in `iconVariants` and, for an inherited entry, the theme that defined the entry lists it too; otherwise it receives `undefined` and draws its normal artwork. `astryx theme build` keeps each inherited entry's defining list, so a built theme passes the same variants as its runtime theme. A `registerIcons()` entry receives the variants the active theme lists, and a node entry ignores `variant`. An icon component passed directly never receives `variant`, and `variant` is never written to the DOM or reflected on the `icon` theming target. Icons without `variant` render as before.
Badge's documentation marks `label` as required, as its props type already does. `astryx component Badge` and the docsite no longer list it as optional.
Keep `Banner` status foreground colors scoped to Banner-owned content so consumer `endContent`, including nested dialogs, retains its own text color.

BottomSheet renders fewer elements, with no visual change: an open sheet's dialog positions the panel itself, the grab bar draws its pill, and a closed sheet renders no edge tint. A switcher's sheets keep their positioner.

`BottomSheet` stacks by open order. A modal sheet opened while another modal sheet is open now stacks on top of it instead of presenting as a second, unrelated dialog: the covered sheet stays mounted with its state, recedes behind the top sheet (0.96 / −8px at depth 1, 0.92 / −16px from depth 2), and is blocked from pointer, keyboard, and assistive technology; only the bottom sheet's backdrop dims the page, so a stack no longer darkens per level; and Escape, a scrim tap, a swipe, and a platform close request pop only the top sheet, through that sheet's own `onOpenChange` and honouring its `purpose`. The top sheet is the most recently opened one still open, wherever the sheets are written — siblings, separate components, inside another sheet's content, or inside a `BottomSheetSwitcher` step; a whole switcher is one level, and switching its step keeps its place. When several sheets open in one update (a deep link), tree order decides and the first painted frame is already right: a sheet nested in another sheet's content no longer opens beneath its parent. Closing the top sheet returns focus into the sheet it reveals; closing every sheet of a stack in one update returns focus once, to the bottom sheet's `finalFocusRef` or opener, after the last dialog has closed (each sheet's own return used to be refused while the others were still modal). A sheet rendered inside a closing sheet's content now leaves with it instead of staying open invisibly, and comes back with the host if its own `isOpen` is still true (its state is never written for it); sheets above it that are not in its content stay open. Sheets with `hasScrim={false}` never stack and are never stacked on. No prop, type, or export changes; a modal sheet on its own behaves exactly as before (apart from the reduced-motion fix released alongside).

BottomSheet follows the reduced-motion design rule. With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, a sheet's entrance, exit, recede and replace handoff — a `BottomSheetSwitcher` step's too — no longer travel or scale: on a touch screen (`pointer: coarse`) the entering sheet fades in at its resting place and the leaving or retained sheet fades out where it is, opacity only, within 200 ms; with a mouse, trackpad or keyboard the change is immediate, except that a swipe dismissal — a transition a touch drag's release started — fades out in place on every pointer. Before, the motions ran shortened transforms on every pointer and nothing cross-faded.

When one standalone `BottomSheet` replaces another and the entering sheet is shorter, the sheet being replaced moves down to the entering sheet's top edge while the entering sheet rises, and only then fades, so the switch reads as one sheet changing height, as a `BottomSheetSwitcher` step change does. It had stayed at its own height and faded out above the entering sheet. Under reduced motion the replaced sheet still does not move.

`BottomSheet` replaces a sheet that closes in the same update another opens. When the top sheet of a stack closes and exactly one other sheet opens in the same update (one state value naming the open step does this), the new sheet replaces it instead of stacking on it: it rises above the replaced sheet, a taller replaced sheet moves down to meet its top edge at the same time, the replaced sheet fades only after both motions finish and is inert and hidden from assistive technology from the start, the scrim holds steady with no dip, focus moves into the new sheet, and closing the flow later returns focus to the element that opened its first sheet. This is the handoff `BottomSheetSwitcher` runs between its steps, now available to standalone sheets; a multi-step flow can be written as one `BottomSheet` per step with no switcher. A covered sheet closing while a sheet opens, several sheets changing at once, or a close and an open in different updates keep the ordinary push and pop motion, and existing stacking behaviour is unchanged. A replace is recognised only when the move was made from inside the closing sheet: the control last pressed (or, with no recent press, the focused element) was in it, as a step's own Continue or Back button is; a close and an open driven from a control outside it, by two unrelated owners, stay a pop and a push with their own focus return. Non-modal sheets (`hasScrim={false}`) replace each other the same way: they are now hosted in the browser top layer as manual popovers, with no scrim, focus trap or scroll lock as before, so a non-modal step orders above the one it replaces, and the toast viewport re-enters the top layer above a non-modal sheet as it does above a modal. The non-modal sheet's page-level `z-index` is gone with the move (AST-027); below the Popover API support floor the sheet falls back to `show()` in page stacking order, usable but with no promise over later page content (the reduced fallback AST-003 describes). They still never stack. A non-modal sheet now also returns focus to its opener when it closes while the person is still in it (a modal sheet always did); focus the person took elsewhere on the live page stays there. The private stack registry now keeps one state per page shared by every copy of the package on it that speaks the same stack protocol version (a copy on another version keeps its own stack), and one stack per document. No prop, type, or export changes; a modal sheet on its own behaves exactly as before (apart from the reduced-motion fix released alongside). A non-modal sheet on its own changes in three ways with its new host: it is in the top layer (a manual popover) instead of page stacking order, its page-level `z-index` is gone, and it returns focus to its opener on close while focus is still inside it; its scrim-less, scroll-free, page-interactive contract is unchanged.

`BottomSheetSwitcher` and the `sheetId` prop of `BottomSheet` are deprecated. The replacement is already in this release: write each step of a multi-step flow as its own standalone `BottomSheet` with `isOpen`, driven by one state value that names the open step; closing the top sheet and opening the next in the same update runs the same replace handoff the switcher ran (entering step above, a taller retained step aligns down and fades after both motions, one steady scrim, focus into the new step and back to the flow's opener on close). Migration, per flow: (1) replace the `activeSheet` / `onActiveSheetChange` pair with one `step` state value; (2) give each step `isOpen={step === 'id'}` and `onOpenChange={isOpen => !isOpen && setStep(current => (current === 'id' ? null : current))}` in place of `sheetId="id"` (the guard keeps a step that is being replaced from clearing the step the person just chose); (3) remove the `BottomSheetSwitcher` wrapper, moving its `hasScrim` onto every step; (4) keep the step buttons as they were (`setStep('next')`). The handoff runs when the move is made from inside the open step (a step's own Continue or Back, or code while focus is in it); a step changed from a control outside the flow's sheets — a page control beside a `hasScrim={false}` flow, or code after focus has left the step — closes and opens with the sheets' own push and pop motion, where the switcher handed off on any `activeSheet` change. The switcher's other props map as follows: `onCancel` becomes a guarded `onOpenChange` on each step (one that ignores `false` while the flow must stay open), which keeps the step's dialog role — a standalone sheet reports Escape, the platform close, the scrim tap and the swipe all as `onOpenChange(false)` with no reason, so the guard holds the step open against all of them while it applies, where `onCancel` vetoed only the cancel request; a veto of Escape alone has no equivalent, and the only per-path lever is `purpose` (`form` keeps Escape and blocks the scrim tap and the swipe; `required` blocks all three and exposes the step as an `alertdialog`). A consumer `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` becomes each step's `label`, which names its dialog. `ref`, `id`, `data-testid`, `className`, `style`, `xstyle` and the other dialog props have no dialog-level equivalent — a standalone sheet's `ref` and base props reach its panel `<div>` and its dialog is implementation — so a test or an anchor that needs the dialog queries the panel's `closest('dialog')`, and dialog-level styling is dropped. Flows that keep using the switcher keep working: a switcher flow used on its own behaves as released — with two fixes released alongside: a toast raised from a step now renders above the flow and can be pressed, and under reduced motion its steps' entrance, exit and handoff follow the reduced-motion rule (no travel; a cross-fade on touch, immediate otherwise) — and when it is stacked with other sheets the stacking behaviour of this release applies to it as one level (it recedes and is blocked when covered, shares the one scrim, stands down from dismissal while covered, and returns focus by the stacking rules). Its declarations and docs are marked `@deprecated` and its docs, templates and stories show only the replacement, until a future minor release removes it. Non-modal flows (`hasScrim={false}`) migrate the same way: non-modal sheets replace each other too.

Toasts raised from a `BottomSheetSwitcher` step stay visible and clickable above the flow. A modal switcher flow now supplies its active step's dialog as the toast viewport's host, as a standalone scrim `BottomSheet` and a `Dialog` do; the host follows each handoff to the entering step, and the flow hands the viewport back when it closes. Before, the viewport stayed behind the flow's dialogs, so a toast raised from a step was covered by the step and a press on it landed on the step. A `hasScrim={false}` flow is not modal and leaves the viewport in place.

Toasts stay visible and clickable above an open BottomSheet. The `ToastViewport` from `LayerProvider` (or the one `useToast` mounts on its own) now moves into a standalone BottomSheet while it is open, as it already does into an open Dialog, and back as soon as the sheet starts closing. Before, the sheet covered the viewport and made it inert, so a click on a toast's action landed on the sheet instead and could dismiss it. A sheet with `hasScrim={false}` is not modal and leaves the viewport in place. Sheets inside a `BottomSheetSwitcher` are unchanged.

BaseTypeahead and CommandPalette: when a typed search finishes before its "Loading" announcement is made, the pending "Loading" is dropped, so a screen reader no longer hears "Loading" after the result count or has it replace the count. This meets the busy-announcement requirement in spec:AST-086 (FR8).

ClickableCard, SelectableCard and an interactive Thumbnail now show the pressed overlay under a finger in apps that compile Astryx from source with cascade layers (the Vite and PostCSS integrations, and Storybook). The touch press was written as an arm of a custom property whose own default sits outside the cascade layer the arm lands in, so the default always won and a touch press painted nothing. The press now paints as the overlay's own image, at the press's strength, and fades at the lift; mouse hover and press are unchanged, and the precompiled stylesheet keeps the same pixels.

`ChatComposer`'s status bar announces through the shared own-content announcement module (`spec:AST-086` FR11–FR13). It still announces errors assertively and warnings politely, once per occasion, but a status that is already showing while the page loads is no longer announced, and it speaks the bar's rendered text without the decorative icon.

Tapping the clear button of a TextInput or NumberInput that is not focused now brings up the iOS keyboard. The field took focus a frame after the tap, and iOS Safari only raises its keyboard for a focus made while handling the touch, so the field ended up focused with no keyboard. The focus now happens inside the tap, still with `preventScroll`, so a scrolled page stays put.

The two Bottom Sheet flow block templates (`BottomSheetSwitcherShowcase`, `BottomSheetSwitcherReviewFlow`) now teach the replacement for the deprecated `BottomSheetSwitcher`: each step is a standalone `BottomSheet` driven by one state value, and moving on replaces the open step in place. Both stay examples of `BottomSheetSwitcher` (the showcase remains that page's hero) and are now also listed under `BottomSheet`. Template ids, files and their published registry identities keep their names, so `template <name>`, the released JSON ids and the ShadCN routes are unchanged.

`detectStylingSystem` recognizes `@stylexjs/unplugin` as a StyleX compiler, so projects compiling StyleX through the standard Vite path are detected as `stylex` instead of falling through to the `css` guidance.

New command `astryx experimental render <page>`: renders a page with your installed Astryx components to ONE self-contained HTML file. The file inlines only the Core CSS rules the page uses plus the page's own StyleX styles and local images, runs no script, loads nothing from the network, follows light and dark mode, and carries the page's source. `astryx experimental render --reverse <file.html>` writes that source back byte for byte, rebuilds a page from Astryx markup when the source was removed, and refuses other HTML. Warnings flag what may not look as meant, such as a `ListItem` given children instead of `label`. Experimental commands live under `astryx experimental`, are marked `[experimental]` in help and the manifest, and may change or be removed in any patch release. Guide: `astryx docs cli/experimental/render-pages`.

Icon sets: authoring a set from a library takes fewer steps and fewer guesses. Only the experimental icon commands, the icon-set guide, and `astryx template` in a project that sets `experimental.iconSet` change; without the opt-in, every stable command reads as before except the `experimental` group's summary in `astryx help` and `astryx manifest`, which now names icon sets: "Try features that may change in a patch release: icon sets (find icons, build an icon-set package)" (it read "Try features that may change or be removed in a patch release").
changesets.body:
- **`experimental icon new-set`.** `--from` maps a definition only when an icon has its exact name and lists those entries for review; other likely icons come back as at most three suggestions per definition, never written. It records the library and version as `source`, copies the library's license notices and takes its license, keeps `--exclude` in the data file's `exclude` for every refresh, and names the exports it left out as not icons. It writes only the set's own files: its receipt names, as text to copy, the entry change that makes the set's icons import from the package by name (never editing a built or CommonJS entry), the `react` and optional `@types/react` and `@astryxdesign/cli` peers, and the `typecheck` script the package is missing, and `integration check` names the same entry change, once, until it is made. `--variants` and `--default-variant` declare variants; `--display-name` and `--description` fill the descriptor, on a refresh too; a refresh that first records the library also copies its license notices and takes its license, and a refresh changes only the icons the refreshed library supplies (your own `./` artwork and other libraries' icons keep their map entries and variants, and `add --all` leaves them alone), knows an existing icon by the library export it re-exports, so the icon keeps its export name exactly, its map entries, variants, and words when its id changes, and the change is listed under `renamed`. Ids keep a dimension as one word (`squares-2x2`), a library's other names for an icon become its words, and `…Provider` and `…Context` exports are never icons. A library of 1,600 icons is read in about two seconds.
- **`experimental icon add` and `map`.** `add --variant <name> --from <module> --all` adds a variant for every icon at once; a `./` file is named as written, and the receipt names the package.json `files` that publishes it. `map --pairs a=b,c=d` writes many entries in one checked write, and both accept a definition's kebab id; `map` names an icon by its id, its export name in any case, or another name its library exports it as, never by one word of its id.
- **Options decided in pairs.** Every icon command refuses two options it would not both honor, with `ERR_INVALID_OPTION` (such as `--list --definitions`, `--definitions --limit 3`, `--all-icons` with a query, `add --all --id`, or `new-set --exclude` without `--from`), instead of ignoring one.
- **All or nothing.** When `new-set`, `add`, `map`, or `new-definition` fails partway, every file is as it was and the error is `ERR_WRITE_FAILED`.
- **Sets named consistently.** Every icon command that names a set (`--set` with a query or `--all-icons`, `<set>/<id>`, `use`, and `add`, `map`, `new-definition` in the package) reports a set that is not there as missing and an invalid one as withdrawn, with why, both `ERR_NOT_FOUND`.
- **Listing.** `experimental icon --set <set> --all-icons` lists every icon of a set (`icon.setIcons`) and `--definitions` lists every Astryx definition, built in or optional (`icon.definitions`). Search shows partial matches only when nothing better matches.
- **Templates.** A mapped icon drops the library's sizing props (`size`, `strokeWidth`, `absoluteStrokeWidth`), reported as `dropped`, and comments on a rewritten import line are kept.
- **Definitions.** Thirteen new icon definitions (`rotate`, `flipHorizontal`, `flipVertical`, `alignStart`, `alignCenter`, `alignEnd`, `panelLeft`, `panelRight`, `gitBranch`, `gitFork`, `scale`, `cpu`, `textCase`), declared by the templates that draw them. Built-in and optional definitions gain common glyph names as words; seven optional definitions lose a word that named a different thing, so a search for that word no longer finds a set's icon through them: `star` (`bookmark`), `database` (`table`), `raiseHand` (`stop`), `redo` (`forward`), `activity` (`monitor`), `archive` (`store`), `mobile` (`device`).
- **Checks.** `integration check` suggests icons by the same rule and lists each optional definition with its description and words; the version-drift warning gives the refresh command.

changesets.headline: The Tokenizer block templates (`Tokenizer`, `Clear`, `Creatable`, `End Content`, `Icon`, `Max Entries`, `Overflow`, `States`) size their field through a column that is 400px wide where there is room and shrinks with its container, instead of a fixed 400px width, so the live examples fit a phone-sized screen without clipping.

The `Tokenizer` showcase block template searches its tags: typing lists the tags that match. Its search source returned nothing for every query, so the live example on the Tokenizer docs page answered all typing with "No results found".

`astryx integration verify` starts npm the way the rest of the CLI does: npm's own entry file, run with the Node that runs the CLI, when one is found. An `npm` earlier on the PATH that is not npm itself, such as a wrapper that refuses npm commands, no longer fails the check with "npm pack failed".

A CodeBlock with no title or language label no longer lets its Copy button cover code. The button sits in its own column beside the code instead of over it, so a long first line ends before the button, whether the code is scrolled sideways, wrapped, or right-to-left. The button is centred on the first line, so a one-line block reads as one row with even space above and below, and a block that grows line by line keeps the button where it was. Blocks with a header are unchanged.

`CodeBlock` takes `endContent`, a slot for your own controls, such as a "Run in terminal" button. They appear just before Copy: in the header when the block has one, otherwise beside the code in the top inline-end corner, never over it. The slot never creates a header, and clicking or pressing keys in it never collapses the block. For single-line mode, leave out the title and pass `hasLanguageLabel={false}`: a one-line command then reads as one row with its controls beside it.
`CodeBlock` highlights C, C++, SQL, Rust, Kotlin, Swift, and Go with no setup.
changesets.body:
Every other language is opt in, one at a time:

- Import that language on its own and pass it as `language`, for example `graphql` from `@astryxdesign/core/CodeBlock/languages/graphql`.
- Modules ship for `graphql`, `java`, `thrift`, `objectiveC` (path `languages/objective-c`), `toml`, `powershell`, `ruby`, `lua`, and `dockerfile`.
- A string such as `language="graphql"` still selects only a built-in language.

Your own languages work the same way. `createCodeLanguage({name, identifiers, fileExtensions, fileNames, tokenize})` makes a language value from your own tokenize function.

The built-in tokenizer stays within 4,608 bytes gzipped. Each module adds at most 512 bytes, and only when you import it.

changesets.headline: The CodeBlock "Code — Snippet" example shows one-line commands with no header. Copy sits beside the code in its own column, so each command reads as a single row. A third block shows a long first line that ends before the button.

CodeBlock's `tokenizer` prop is deprecated in favour of a custom language value: pass `language={createCodeLanguage({name, identifiers, tokenize})}` with the same function. The prop still works exactly as released. `astryx upgrade` rewrites it when it sits beside a static `language`. A function literal becomes `language={createCodeLanguage({name: 'zig', identifiers: ['zig'], tokenize: (code) => …})}`. A name or call-free property becomes `language={fn ? createCodeLanguage({…, tokenize: fn}) : 'zig'}`, since it may be undefined. Uses it cannot prove are left unchanged, with a TODO comment: a computed, missing, or `plaintext` language, any other tokenizer value, or a block that spreads props.

`astryx upgrade` no longer fails when a protected file (vendored, generated, or ignored) does not parse, such as a vendored bundle written for another toolchain. It skips the file, lists it under `declinedCandidates` with the parse error's location, and completes the rest of the upgrade. A file upgrade owns that does not parse still fails the run, and protected files that parse are still checked and reported.

`astryx upgrade` no longer scans through a symbolic link into installed dependencies or version-control metadata, such as a symlinked `node_modules` or a link into a package store. Those trees were already never written; skipping them stops a run from the project root spending minutes reading them. Other symbolically linked folders are still scanned so their required changes are reported.

CommandPaletteEmpty wraps a long unbroken word, such as a file path or URL in an empty-search message, inside the palette instead of spilling it past both edges where its start and end could not be read.

ComplexSelector: the trigger is now a combobox whose popup is a dialog, so a screen reader hears when the field is required (`aria-required` was ignored on the old button role). With `renderTrigger`, the caller's control receives the same `role`, `aria-required`, and `aria-disabled`, is named by `label` unless the selector is given `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and a disabled control keeps its tab stop but does not open. Button keeps a caller-supplied `aria-disabled` and `aria-busy`, so a Button used as that control carries the selector's state. Tests that find the trigger with `getByRole('button')` should use `getByRole('combobox')`.

ComplexSelector: a caller's `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` now names the built-in trigger, replacing the field label, as it already did for a `renderTrigger` control. Before, the built-in trigger always took its name from the label, so a name passed to the selector was never announced.

A ContextMenu opened by a finger's long press stays open as the finger lifts: the compatibility `mousedown` the browser sends for that press as it lifts no longer reads as a press outside. Every other press outside the menu closes it, or leaves it open, as before.

Internal: a shared touch hit-area utility (utils/hitArea.ts) that grows a target toward 44 px under a coarse pointer and stops at half the gap to each neighbour, so a tap goes to the nearer target. Not exported.

`astryx upgrade --from` a version before 0.7.0 no longer fails on `var(--color-data-*)` uses without a fallback. Prebuilt `@astryxdesign/core/astryx.css` defines all 56 data-color defaults, and source builds read data colors through `dataVars`, so the upgrade no longer asks for fallbacks. A graph-based source build, such as `@astryxdesign/build/vite`, that reads raw `var(--color-data-*)` strings without a `dataVars` import should import `dataVars` from `@astryxdesign/core/theme/dataTokens.stylex`; the upgrade no longer reports those uses. Stale generated theme CSS that still emits the defaults at `:root` still fails the upgrade.

Dialog: with reduced motion on a touch screen, the dialog fades in where it lands, in 200 ms or less, instead of appearing with no transition. With a mouse it still appears at once, and it never slides or scales in under reduced motion (design:reduced-motion).

A process that calls the CLI API more than once, such as a docs site's search or an agent harness, now sees an edit to a doc file it already read: `search()`, `docs()` and `component()` read the edited file's new content on their next call, instead of what the process first imported. An unchanged doc file is still imported once and shared, so readers keep getting the module's own doc.

`DropdownMenuRadioItem` now runs a caller's `onClick` and `onPointerMove`. Before, the row's own selection and hover-focus handlers replaced them, so they never ran. They now run after the row selects its value and takes hover focus, as they already do on `DropdownMenuItem` and `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem`; a disabled row still selects nothing and does not call `onClick`. The documentation also marks `value` and `label` as required and no longer says disabled radio items stay reachable with the arrow keys, which DropdownMenu currently skips.

`DropdownMenuSubMenu`'s documentation marks `label` and `children` as required, as its props type already does, and documents `menuDataTestId`, the test id for the sub-menu's own menu (the flyout, or the drilled-in list on a phone). The `presentation` prop's JSDoc now declares its `'adaptive'` default.

Internal: DropdownMenu's rule that steps the root menu aside while a sub-menu's drilled-in view shows names its surface host by an internal marker instead of a universal selector. No visible or behavior change.

New `--ease-exit` token, `cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0.6, 0.6)`: an accelerating curve for things leaving the screen, beside `--ease-standard` for things arriving. `BottomSheet` closes on it at the value it already used, so nothing looks different; a theme can now retune that exit through the token. On a touch screen the sheet keeps its own closing curve. `astryx docs motion`, the easing token table, and the theme template list it. (#8004)
Internal: a menu's edge autoscroll runs on a shared edge-autoscroll timer (utils/edgeAutoscroll.ts), with the same zone, step and interval as before. No behavior change.

EmptyState's root no longer carries `role="status"`, so it is not a live region that mounts already holding its text, which screen readers announce unreliably (`spec:AST-086` FR2). Apps need no code change. An EmptyState rendered or changed while the page loads announces nothing; one that appears later, or whose title or description changes later, announces its title and description once through the shared polite live region; inside a live container such as `ChatMessageList`'s log, the container announces it (`spec:AST-086` FR4). A `role` you pass now reaches the root instead of being replaced; tests that found EmptyState with `getByRole('status')` need another selector.

A component family lists the same members whether or not its package has been built. When the package's `exports` give a `source` condition and that file is in the package, the CLI reads the family's members from it instead of from the built output. Before, a member that only the package's entry exports, such as Lab's `TourStep`, was listed only after a local build. The official package list now includes `TourStep`.

FileInput: clearing the selection returns focus to the file-selection trigger. Before, both keyboard and pointer activation of the clear button focused the visually hidden native `<input type="file">`, which is `aria-hidden` and out of the tab order, so a screen reader announced nothing after the clear. Now focus lands on the trigger, which announces the field label. No API changes.
Internal: the pan gesture recognizer, with UIKit's measured hysteresis and velocity filter. Not exported from the package entry point; no component uses it yet.

Internal: the gesture recognizer core for touch presentations: UIKit's recognizer state machine and the arena that settles which recognizer owns a touch. Not exported from the package entry point; no component uses it yet.
Internal: tap and long-press gesture recognizers with UIKit's measured thresholds. Not exported from the package entry point; no component uses them yet.

Tooltip and HoverCard answer a touch only once it is a tap. On a touch screen they used to open as soon as a finger landed on a trigger that performs no action, so a scroll that started on an info icon or an abbreviation opened its tooltip and left it open, and a finger resting on the trigger opened it too. Now the tap opens the layer when the finger lifts, and a touch that turns into a scroll never opens it, the way a tap on iOS behaves. A tap-opened tooltip or card closes when a tap outside lifts, or as soon as a scroll that starts outside takes the touch, which is when iOS dismisses a popover; before, it closed the moment a finger landed anywhere else. Triggers that perform an action keep their tap, and `touchTrigger` keeps its meaning.

A theme sets the dimension of each Icon size: `width` and `height` in `px` or `rem` on `components.icon['size:sm']` (or `xsm`, `md`, `lg`) resize that size's glyph, for semantic icon names and for SVG components passed to `Icon`, in runtime and built themes alike. Before, those properties sized the box around a semantic icon but not its 1em artwork, and an app that compiles StyleX without CSS layers let the icon's own size win over the theme. A size the theme does not style still renders at 12, 16, 20, or 24px at a 16px root and scales with the root font size. `astryx docs theme` gains an Icon sizes section.
Internal: InputGroup's edge rules name group members by an internal marker instead of a universal selector. No visible or behavior change.

A row with `swipeActions` no longer blocks pinch-zoom. A pinch that started on a swipeable `Item` or `ListItem` did nothing, because the row declared `touch-action: pan-y`, and a sideways pinch could also be taken as a swipe. The row now leaves pinch to the browser (`pan-y pinch-zoom`), and a second finger that lands before the swipe has begun, on the row or anywhere else, hands the touch to the browser, so the page zooms and the row stays where it is. One-finger swipes and vertical scrolling are unchanged.

Pages with many closed popovers, tooltips and menus mount faster. A layer that renders closed outside an inline or interactive parent no longer reads computed style when it mounts; it reads its writing direction when it first opens, before its first frame. On a page with hundreds of closed layers, each of those mount-time reads forced its own style recalculation. Open layers look and behave as before, in right-to-left and vertical text too.

useLayer: placing a context layer no longer re-renders its host. The hook still resolves where the layer goes from its inert marker once the marker is in the DOM, but it now hands that mount to an internal slot that renders the marker and the layer, so the render that places the layer is the slot's alone. A Tooltip, Selector or ComplexSelector that mounts closed renders once; a Popover or DropdownMenu keeps only the renders its own state costs. The host still renders when a resolved mount is replaced by a render call that moved to another host. The DOM, server markup, hydration and `lazyMount` are unchanged.

With Reduce Motion on, a Tooltip, HoverCard, Popover, menu or other layer that opens under a finger now fades in, with no slide and no scale, in 200 ms or less, instead of appearing at once. Under a mouse it still appears at once, and without Reduce Motion the entrance is unchanged.

`astryx upgrade` no longer reports an error on an `astryx.config` written as `const config = {...}; export default config;`, the shape generated configs use. The `migrate-layout-components-to-experimental` codemod now follows a default-exported identifier to its top-level `const` binding when the binding is not exported any other way and nothing else references it, so a config without `layout` is left unchanged and one with `layout.components` is migrated.

`Layout` no longer ships a `:has()` on the layout followed by a universal `*` selector for the padding that collapses next to a `LayoutHeader` or `LayoutFooter` without a divider. That selector shape can make a browser restyle everything inside the layout on each change within it, which costs the most in long documents. `LayoutHeader` and `LayoutFooter` now carry internal markers, and Layout's middle row reads them with sibling selectors. Rendering is unchanged for a Layout's own content, and a Layout nested in another Layout's content or panels still inherits the outer collapse. One case changes: a Layout nested inside a `LayoutHeader` or `LayoutFooter` that has no divider no longer takes that outer collapse, so its content keeps its own inner padding beside its own divider (16px at the default spacing) instead of 0px.
Lightbox: the viewer is as tall as the visible viewport (`100dvh`), so on an iPhone Safari's bottom toolbar no longer covers its bottom, where a gallery's caption sits.
Lightbox: a viewer opened before its first item arrives now opens when that item does. It used to stay closed, its dialog never shown.

Lightbox's Left and Right arrow keys now follow the writing direction. In a right-to-left page the gallery's Next button sits on the left, and ArrowLeft now moves to the next item and ArrowRight to the previous one, matching the buttons. Before, ArrowLeft always went to the previous item, so in RTL the keys moved against their buttons. Panning a zoomed image with the arrow keys is unchanged in both directions: the image is not mirrored, so ArrowRight still reveals what is to its right.

`ListItem`'s documentation says what `isSelected` does: it marks the row as the current item with `aria-current="true"`. It used to say `aria-selected`, which a list item cannot carry and which the component has not set since 0.1.9.

Numbered List and Markdown markers end on one edge, with tabular figures, so every period in a list lines up as native list markers do. In List, a counter wider than its marker hangs toward the start before it widens the shared column. Markdown's non-swipe document lists instead keep the ordinary text inset and let whole counters paint outside it, matching RichText's native outside markers even beyond the marker gutter. Single-digit numbers, now right-aligned in their marker, sit a few pixels closer to their text.

Keep multi-digit List and Markdown counters on one line in a shared number column, so sibling text and nested lists stay aligned. Bullets and the text inset of short-only lists without task items retain their existing spacing; numbered rows beside task items move to share the checkbox's text start. Short numbers are right-aligned in their marker, moving the digits a few pixels closer to their text. Markdown task lists with nested or other block content place each checkbox on its item's first line and name it by that item's own text, instead of centering it against the whole body and naming it by all nested content inside a “Task list” group; those lists retain list semantics without that extra group. Paragraph-only pure task lists are unchanged. Browsers without CSS subgrid keep readable, unbroken counters in the existing flex layout, without the shared-column alignment enhancement.
Localize pasted-text counts, spoken shortcut names and Ctrl/Esc keycaps; format file-size limits with provider-locale digits and translatable units
`astryx component <name>` now suggests a component whose whole name is part of the typed name (a wrapper or prefixed name) when nothing else matches, instead of no suggestions.

When `astryx component`, `astryx template` or `astryx docs` names nothing, the suggestions now stop where the matches get weaker, so a strong first suggestion is no longer followed by unrelated entries. A component list keeps its first two suggestions and, after them, only suggestions about as close as the first or a close spelling of the whole typed name. In a template list, and in the docs list for an unknown topic that is not a route, when the closest entry carries every typed word, only entries that carry every typed word stay; when it carries some of them, entries that carry none are left out. One-letter words do not count. A name that shares no word with any entry still gets the full list, and an unknown route still suggests every child of its namespace. Lists only get shorter, and every suggestion still names a real entry.

`Markdown` takes `codeLanguages`, a list of CodeBlock language values, each imported on its own or made with `createCodeLanguage`. A fence whose language word names a listed value renders with that value, ahead of a built-in language with the same name. A `diff-<name>` fence gets the diff layer over that value.

Markdown's FR23 performance bench times each sampling window on the calling thread's CPU clock instead of the whole process's, so CPU spent by V8's background threads or a worker no longer counts toward either side. Test-only; `Markdown`'s behavior does not change.

DropdownMenu, ContextMenu: after a pointer press, a row the mouse rests on, or a held press is dragged over, takes focus without matching `:focus-visible`. A plain focus inherited the state from the focus before it (the menu after a pointer open), so any keyboard-only focus style, a theme's or an app's, painted on the row under the mouse. That focus now follows the last input, as other programmatic focus in Astryx does: after a keyboard open, or a key press, the indicator stays. Checkbox, radio and sub-menu rows, and the ContextMenu and Breadcrumbs menus built on them, follow. Browsers without the focus option (Chrome and Edge before 145, Safari before 18.4) keep the earlier behavior.

DropdownMenu, MoreMenu and ContextMenu: a menu presented as a bottom sheet (`presentation="bottom-sheet"`, or `"adaptive"` on a phone) no longer keeps its closed sheet and every item mounted while the menu is closed. The sheet mounts as it opens and unmounts after its exit, with focus still returning to the trigger. The open sheet also renders two fewer wrapper elements, with the same layout.
Point package metadata and project links at the `meta/astryx` repository.

`astryx upgrade` to 0.7 no longer rewrites an app's own class on MetadataList, such as `.astryx-metadata-list.app-compact-list`, into a `[data-columns="app-compact-list"]` selector that never matches. Only the column values MetadataList emitted (`single`, `multi`, and `columns-<n>`) become `data-columns` selectors. (#7982)

`MobileNav` is never wider than 85% of the viewport, as its `width` documentation says. A 320 px drawer on a 320 px phone used to cover the whole screen and leave no backdrop to tap; it is now 272 px wide and leaves a 48 px strip of the page beside it, and a tap on that strip closes it. On wider screens the drawer keeps its `width`.
`astryx discover` lists the experimental MobilePowerSearch component from `@astryxdesign/lab`. (#7983)

MultiSelector: a caller's `aria-labelledby` now reaches the built-in trigger. Before, MultiSelector replaced it with its own value, so the trigger lost the extra name (standalone it had no `aria-labelledby` at all). Now the caller's ids follow the field's own label: `label="Fruits" aria-labelledby="lunch-heading"` names the trigger "Fruits Lunch", and inside an InputGroup the group label comes first. With `renderTrigger`, the caller's control still receives the caller's `aria-labelledby` as given. Triggers without a caller `aria-labelledby` are unchanged. No API changes.

A disabled `NavHeadingMenuItem` with `href` no longer navigates (`spec:AST-085` FR2). Before, it kept its link destination and only skipped `onClick`, so a click, a middle-click, or assistive-technology activation still followed the link. It now renders a plain `<a>` with no `href`, still reports `aria-disabled`, and does not use a custom `LinkProvider` component. The disabled link row now carries `tabIndex={-1}`: it stays focusable but is no longer a Tab stop (before, it was a page Tab stop only because it kept its `href`; `spec:AST-085` FR1). A link row that becomes disabled or enabled while focused keeps focus (`spec:AST-085` FR4). Apps need no code change; an enabled item is unchanged.

A mouse slide across the items of NavHeadingMenu or TabMenu no longer selects their text. In an expanded SideNavHeading, which stays open after a pick, the selection used to stay on the item the press began on. Caller content beside NavHeadingMenu's items stays selectable.

NavHeadingMenu, TopNavMenu, SideNavHeading's menu, TopNavHeading's product menu, BreadcrumbItem's menu and TabMenu track a held pointer across their items, as DropdownMenu does: a press (finger, pen or mouse) that slides across the items acts on the one it lifts on, once, with the highlight following the pointer, and a mouse released outside closes the menu. A link item is no longer draggable, so a mouse press that slides to another item is not a drag. Keyboard and assistive-technology behavior is unchanged. No API changes.

NumberInput: a caller's `aria-labelledby` now reaches the input. Before, NumberInput replaced it with its own value, so the input lost the extra name (standalone it had no `aria-labelledby` at all). Now the caller's ids follow the field's own label: `label="Amount" aria-labelledby="shipping-heading"` names the input "Amount Shipping", and inside an InputGroup the group label comes first. Inputs without a caller `aria-labelledby` are unchanged. No API changes.

NumberInput: a disabled field now keeps its place in the tab order, so keyboard and screen-reader users can reach it and hear that it is unavailable (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value and 2.4.7 Focus Visible; `spec:AST-085` FR1–FR3 and FR6). It exposes `aria-disabled="true"` and is read-only instead of carrying the native `disabled` attribute, as it already did with a `disabledMessage`; it is still dimmed, cannot be edited or stepped, and is left out of form submission. Like a natively disabled field, it runs no caller event handler other than focus and blur, and Enter does not submit its form. Its number steppers expose `aria-disabled` too, and under keyboard focus the field shows its focus ring, dimmed with the rest of the field. The Pagination page box follows.

`Overlay`, `DropdownMenuGroup` and `MobileNavToggle` now forward host attributes and DOM handlers (`id`, `data-*`, `aria-*`, event handlers) to the element each one owns, as other DOM-owning components do. Before, `Overlay` and `DropdownMenuGroup` accepted only `xstyle`, `className`, `style` and `ref` and dropped everything else, so a test id or analytics attribute on either never reached the page; `MobileNavToggle` also forwarded `data-testid`, but no other `data-*`, `id`, `aria-*` or handler. Built-in behavior stays component-owned: `Overlay`'s touch toggle and `MobileNavToggle`'s drawer toggle run on every press, before a caller handler; `DropdownMenuGroup` keeps its `role="group"` and, while it has a `title`, keeps that title as its name; `MobileNavToggle` keeps its `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.

usePopover: a popover that closes or unmounts before its first frame no longer moves focus into its hidden content. Auto-focus waits a frame for the content to mount, and that frame is now cancelled with the open, so pressing Escape right after opening a Popover or a collapsed SideNav submenu leaves focus on the trigger.

Popover: an open popover no longer pulls in a Tab pressed elsewhere on the page. Keyboard users can move through the rest of the page in order while a popover is open, for example a list next to a non-modal comment popover. Focus inside the popover still cycles with Tab and Shift+Tab, and Escape still closes it and returns focus to its trigger. `useFocusTrap` applies the same rule: it holds focus that is inside its container and leaves Tabs that start outside to the page. This meets `component:Popover` DEC-9. Fixes #7687.

Popover takes `presentation`, with the values DropdownMenu and Selector use: `'popover'` (the default, unchanged) anchors it to its trigger, `'bottom-sheet'` presents its content in a modal BottomSheet labeled by `label`, and `'adaptive'` uses the BottomSheet on a compact touch screen (a phone) and the anchored popover elsewhere, the way iOS presents a popover on an iPhone. Compact is the theme's compact definition: narrower than its `md` width point or shorter than 500 px. In a sheet, `placement`, `alignment`, `width`, `role`, `isModal` and `hasAutoFocus` do not apply, and `xstyle`, `className` and `style` style the sheet's panel. The sheet loads only when a popover can present one.

A `Popover` rendered into a second document through a portal, such as a same-origin iframe or a Document Picture-in-Picture window, now focuses its first control on open, keeps Tab inside, closes on Escape, and returns focus to its trigger, as it does in the page. Its trigger there stays the popover's invoker `source`.

PowerSearch no longer announces its initial `resultCount` on mount under React StrictMode. The result-count live-region effect guarded its first run with a mounted flag that StrictMode's effect replay reset, so the count present on mount was spoken unprompted; the guard now compares against the last announced text, so only a change after mount is announced in every render mode.

On a phone or tablet, a press made with a mouse, a trackpad or the Space key now shows the pressed state. Touch devices drop the CSS `:active` press so a finger only sees the touch press model, but that rule keys on the device's primary pointer, so a tablet with a trackpad and keyboard (or a phone with a mouse) lost the pressed state for every press that was not a finger. The touch press controller now paints those presses on such devices with the same pixels a desktop press has: at once, held while the button or key is down, faded at the release. As on a desktop, Space paints only a focused button that is itself the pressed surface (a checkbox's or radio's row stays at rest), and a menu row keeps the menu's own highlight. Desktop presses and finger presses are unchanged.
Published type declarations use fully specified relative imports, so projects compiled with `moduleResolution: NodeNext` resolve them (#7702)

`RadioList`'s pressed circle no longer comes from a `:has()` check that reached every element under the row, so a large page no longer restyles everything under each row whenever anything inside it changes. The row is pressed and the circle shows it exactly as before, and a link or button inside the row still keeps its own press.

Internal: the motion foundation has one release policy, `motion/resolveSnapPoint.ts` (where a release lands: a flick goes at least to the next snap point, a release moving back toward its start cancels to it), on the `selectSnapPoint` primitive; paging moves to `motion/selectPage.ts` on top of it. No behavior change.

In `RichTextEditor` and `RichTextView`, a code block that names no language now leaves room for its corner Copy button. A long line wraps before the button instead of running under it. The block is as tall as the same fence in `Markdown`, so switching between reading and editing no longer moves the content below it.

`RichTextEditor` and `RichTextView` take `codeLanguages`, the same list of CodeBlock language values that `Markdown` takes. A fence named by a listed value is coloured with that value and labelled with its name, so reading and editing match.

Scrolling a `ScrollableArea`, or any viewport that uses `useScrollableArea` (Table, CodeBlock, BottomSheet's body), no longer reads computed style on each frame. Before, every scroll event triggered a full measurement in the next animation frame: four computed-style reads plus geometry. When something else on the page had changed style earlier in that frame, this forced a style recalculation from script. Now the scroll event works out the logical edges from box geometry alone, with no computed style and no frame request. Size, style and writing-mode changes still trigger a full measurement, at most once per frame, and so does a scroll whose offset the measured writing direction rules out (a direction changed by a stylesheet alone).

Internal: the UIKit scroll table's scroll-to-top note says that under Reduce Motion a tap-started scroll to the top cross-fades on a coarse pointer and jumps otherwise, since only momentum after a throw keeps decaying. No behavior change.

A scroll viewport that owns keyboard access (`ScrollableArea`, and the Table, CodeBlock, BottomSheet and Schedule viewports built on the same hook) is a tab stop from the first frame its content overflows. Content that arrived already overflowing, such as loaded data replacing a loading state, used to scroll for at least one animation frame, and longer on a busy page, before the viewport joined the tab order. During that time a keyboard user could not reach it and an accessibility audit reported `scrollable-region-focusable`.

On touch screens, `ScrollableArea` keeps the platform's own scroll indicator. Its neutral `scrollbar-color` replaced iOS Safari's indicator with a faint bar that was hard to see while scrolling and also showed in the gap a pull opens; iOS now draws its own indicator, only while scrolling. Mouse and trackpad scrollbars keep the neutral colour. To keep the neutral colour on touch screens too, set `scrollbarColor` through the `xstyle` prop.

SegmentedControl keeps a caller's `aria-describedby`. The radiogroup always replaced it with the disabled-reason tooltip id, or removed it when no reason showed, so the caller's ids never reached the accessible description. The group is now described by the caller's ids and then the disabled reason, the same order RadioList uses.

SelectableCard's guidance no longer recommends it for single-select groups. Each card is a checkbox, so a single-select set built from it is announced as multi-select, with one tab stop per card and no arrow-key navigation between them. Its guidance now covers multi-select groups only.

Selector: a caller's `aria-labelledby` now reaches the trigger. Before, Selector replaced it with its own value, so the trigger lost the extra name (standalone it had no `aria-labelledby` at all). Now the caller's ids follow the field's own label: `label="Fruit" aria-labelledby="lunch-heading"` names the trigger "Fruit Lunch", and inside an InputGroup the group label comes first. Triggers without a caller `aria-labelledby` are unchanged. No API changes.

Selector's touch sheet no longer points screen readers at an option that isn't there yet. On the first open in the bottom-sheet presentation, the trigger used to report the active option (`aria-activedescendant`) while the sheet was still loading and none of its options existed. The trigger now names the active option only once the sheet has rendered it.

SideNav: a collapsed rail item's tooltip now binds to the link or button itself rather than the row around it, so the focusable control is the WAI-ARIA tooltip pattern's trigger and is described by the tooltip (`aria-describedby`) from its first render. Keyboard focus on it now shows the label. As with other link and button tooltips, a touch tap activates the control without opening the tooltip. A disabled item still shows its label on hover.

SideNavHeading: with `headingHref` as its only link, `headerEndContent` now renders beside the heading link instead of inside it. A button placed there was nested in the link, so pressing it also followed the link. The link's accessible name no longer includes the end content.

SideNav's rail no longer snaps when it collapses or expands. Layout snaps to the new width at once, the rail covers or reveals its labels with a clip and ends in its real collapsed state, and inside AppShell the content slides with it, its old line wrapping fading out over the new one, all on one motion (`springs.settle`). Under Reduce Motion it cross-fades with a finger and changes at once otherwise. Nothing animates a width, and no new props.

Skeleton keeps pulsing in Safari while a script runs. Its stepped pulse used a `steps()` timing function, which Safari never animates off the main thread, so the placeholders froze for as long as the page ran JavaScript; Chromium and Firefox were unaffected. The same ten steps are now written as keyframes with a linear timing function, which every engine animates on its compositor. The pulse looks and times exactly as before, including its stagger and reduced-motion behavior.

Slider keeps a caller's `aria-labelledby`. The thumb of a single slider and the group of a range slider always replaced it with the label id, so the caller's ids never reached the accessible name. The control is now named by its label and then the caller's ids, the same order RadioList and TimeInput use.

Slider: the document listener that ends a drag when its pointer capture is lost now exists only while a drag is in progress, so an idle slider no longer holds a document-level listener for its whole lifetime. A drag still ends when the control is replaced mid-drag (a FormLayout direction change).

Slider: a drag belongs to the pointer that started it. A second finger that lands on the slider, moves or lifts during a drag no longer moves the value, takes over the drag or ends it, and two fingers can still drag two sliders at once. A drag whose pointer capture is lost without a pointer up also ends, with one `onChangeEnd`, so the slider keeps answering new presses. Introduced in #8152; final-state evidence (#8284).

Status colours now have a role for each surface, and Info is a new status. For each of info, success, warning, and error: `--color-<status>` is the strong fill and `--color-on-<status>` is content on it, at 4.5:1 or more; `--color-<status>-muted` is the pale fill, with `--color-on-<status>-muted` content; and `--color-text-<status>` is readable status text on the page and cards, with `--color-icon-<status>` and `--color-border-<status>` (status icons and borders) defaulting to it. `--color-info`, `--color-on-info`, `--color-info-muted`, and the other Info roles are new and independent of the accent. Tailwind gains `bg-info`, `bg-info-muted`, `text-on-<status>`, `text-on-<status>-muted`, and `text-status-<status>` (the status text role). Introduced in #7657; final-state evidence (#8729).
changesets.body:
`--color-success`, `--color-warning`, and `--color-error` and `bg-<status>` keep their meaning as the strong fills. Tailwind now projects each status by paint property: `text-`, `decoration-`, `placeholder-`, and `caret-<status>` read the status text role, and `border-`, `divide-`, `outline-`, and `ring-<status>` read the status border role, so status text and lines are readable on the page; `bg-`, `accent-`, `fill-`, `stroke-<status>`, shadow colours, and gradients keep the strong fill. for example, Core's light `text-warning` is now `#753F07` instead of `#E9AF08`, and `text-success` is `#09441F` instead of `#0D8626`. To keep the fill colour on text, use `text-[var(--color-warning)]`.

What changes on screen:

- Core's dark Error content (`--color-on-error`) is now `#0A1317` instead of white, so text on dark-mode error fills reaches 4.5:1. Core's Info Badge uses `--color-info` (`#0064E0`) instead of the accent; in dark mode the accent was `#2694FE`.
- Icon `color="info|success|warning|error"`, Stepper status glyphs, and Chat tool-call status icons use the icon roles, which are the readable text colours. For example, Core's success icon is now `#09441F` (light) instead of `#0D8626`.
- Input and FileInput status borders use the border roles. Core's light warning border is now `#753F07` instead of `#E9AF08`. Butter's light success and warning input rims are now mid-ramp stops that reach 3:1.
- Banner paints its built-in title, description, icon, and controls with the on-muted roles, and fills Info with `--color-info-muted`.
- Status fills keep a visible boundary in forced-colors mode.
- Chocolate and Matcha's `--color-on-success` and `--color-on-error` are now a dark ink instead of white, and Stone's `--color-on-success`, `--color-on-warning` and `--color-on-error` are white in light mode and near-black in dark mode instead of the status hue, so content on those fills reaches 4.5:1.
- Neutral's `--color-success`, `--color-warning`, and `--color-error` are now its status fills, the colours its Badges already showed: success `#00490B` to `#198100` (dark `#A4D6A3` to `#64AF4C`), warning `#4B3900` to `#FFCE2F` (dark `#F8D36A` to `#FFCE2F`), and error `#76000C` to `#C9303A` (dark `#FFC4BE` to `#FF705D`); `--color-info` is `#0074E2` (dark `#6D9CFE`). Its Badges, StatusDots, progress fills, and Stepper badges look the same, and its `text-<status>` utilities read its status text roles.
- Neutral drops its own status overrides and uses the standard roles: the accent variants of ProgressBar, StatusDot, and Stepper now paint Neutral's accent instead of blue, and Banner and the pale destructive Button use the standard overlays. Neutral no longer defines its proposed and undocumented local tokens; use the standard roles instead: `--astryx-theme-neutral-color-status-fill-success`, `-status-fill-warning`, and `-status-fill-error` → `--color-success`, `--color-warning`, `--color-error`; `-status-muted-accent` → `--color-info-muted`; `-on-tint-neutral` → `--color-neutral`; `-on-tint-overlay-hover`, `-on-tint-overlay-pressed`, `-destructive-overlay-hover`, and `-destructive-overlay-pressed` → `--color-overlay-hover` and `--color-overlay-pressed`. `--astryx-theme-neutral-color-status-fill-accent` keeps its value for Neutral extensions but is deprecated and no longer used by Neutral.
- Every first-party theme sets a blue `--color-info`; Chocolate and Matcha Info Badges move from the accent to that blue (Butter keeps its own Info Badge colours).

Custom themes get the content and text roles they don't set: theme generation derives `--color-on-<status>` (light or dark content, whichever contrasts more), readable status text, and on-muted content from the theme's status fills. To keep a component's previous colour, set the matching role in your theme; for example, set `--color-icon-success` to your old `--color-success` value.

changesets.headline: Step: a clickable step's number badge and label are no longer adjacent text, so a text reading of the button no longer joins them as "1Account" (axe-core 4.14's Label in Name rule reported every clickable numbered step). A whitespace node now separates them in all four layouts; the rows are flex containers, so nothing changes on screen. A step's `description` inside the button is a separate Label in Name case and is unchanged.

`Switch`'s focus ring now follows the switch's own input through a sibling selector instead of a `:has()` check on the whole row, so a switch whose row holds large content (a long description, for example) no longer restyles everything in that row whenever something inside it changes. The ring looks and behaves the same. One edge changes: a focusable link inside the switch's label or description keeps its own focus ring and no longer also rings the switch.

TabList's description no longer promises a built-in "more" menu: a strip narrower than its tabs scrolls horizontally and keeps the selected tab in view (`TabMenu` stays the way to group extra options). The library page template describes `MobileNav` as the slide-out navigation drawer it is, not as a bottom tab bar.

In TabList's default `hug` layout, a `Tab` and a `TabMenu` trigger no longer shrink below their labels. On a page whose CSS lets flex items shrink below their content (a `min-width: 0` reset), a narrow strip squeezed its stops until the labels drew over one another, before overflow could scroll. Each hugging stop now keeps its width and the strip scrolls, as its overflow handling intends; `fill` tabs still share the strip.

Table: a pinned column (`useTableStickyColumns`) now draws its own row dividers, so the line under it no longer goes missing while the table scrolls horizontally. A theme's border color and an app's own borders on a row or cell carry onto the pinned cells, and an open detail panel (`useTableRowExpansion`) carries its row's divider the same way.

Table: `useTableRowExpansion` takes an `animatedLayout` handle from `useAnimatedLayout`. With it, opening or closing a row's panel glides the rows after it to their new places instead of jumping, and each row's divider moves with its row. Under Reduce Motion the rows fade in place on a touch screen and change at once with a mouse; in a table with column lines (`dividers="columns"` or `"grid"`) they change at once.

TextInput, TextArea: a disabled field now keeps its place in the tab order, so keyboard and screen-reader users can reach it and hear that it is unavailable (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value and 2.4.7 Focus Visible; `spec:AST-085` FR1–FR3 and FR6). It exposes `aria-disabled="true"` and is read-only instead of carrying the native `disabled` attribute, as the field already did when a `disabledMessage` was set. It is still dimmed, cannot be edited, and is left out of form submission. Like a natively disabled field, it runs no caller event handler other than focus and blur, and Enter in a disabled TextInput does not submit its form. Under keyboard focus it shows the field's focus ring, dimmed with the rest of the field.

TextInput: a caller's `aria-labelledby` now reaches the input. Before, TextInput replaced it with its own value, so the input lost the extra name (standalone it had no `aria-labelledby` at all). Now the caller's ids follow the field's own label: `label="Email" aria-labelledby="billing-heading"` names the input "Email Billing", and inside an InputGroup the group label comes first. Inputs without a caller `aria-labelledby` are unchanged. No API changes.

`astryx theme build` reports a theme module that fails to load (an import it cannot resolve, or an error it throws) instead of building the theme from the text of its `defineTheme()` or default-export object; a theme module whose default export is a plain object builds as before, and a theme outside a project that imports Core builds with the Core the CLI answers with.

`astryx theme build` fails, naming it and its import error, when the project's installed `@astryxdesign/core` (or, outside a project, the Core the CLI release carries) does not load or lacks `defineTheme` or `generateThemeRulesSplit`, instead of building with the CLI's own Core. A project with no Core installed still builds with the CLI's.

`@astryxdesign/core/theme` exports the compact definition: `compactDefinition(widthBreakpoints?)` and `DEFAULT_COMPACT_DEFINITION`. A screen is compact while its viewport is narrower than the theme's `md` point (768 by default) or shorter than 500. The definition carries both edges and ready-made media queries, with and without a coarse pointer, so every component that picks a presentation by screen size reads one shared definition. Nothing changes behavior yet.

The theme authoring guide, and the comment in the theme file `astryx init` and `astryx theme template` write, say an extending theme's `motion` inherits field by field: the child's `fast`, `medium` and `ratio` regenerate the fast and medium duration tokens, and `slow` or `easing` left unset keep the base theme's tokens (an inherited slow band stays at the base's ratio). It used to say the child's motion config replaced the base's entirely.

`astryx upgrade` to 0.7 no longer renames component keys in a look-alike theme object that is not an Astryx theme, such as another library's `{name, components: {checkbox, radio, textarea}}` theme. A theme object with no `defineTheme()` call or Astryx theme type is migrated only when it is the binding a same-stem theme descriptor declares (`brandTheme` exported from `brandTheme.ts` beside `brandTheme.doc.mjs`). (#7980)

Thumbnail: Open and Remove stay mounted while they cannot act. A loading or disabled thumbnail keeps Open, and a disabled one keeps Remove, focusable and announced as disabled instead of removing them, so keyboard focus on an action no longer falls to the page body when the thumbnail starts loading or becomes disabled.

Thumbnail — Disabled block: its description no longer says the remove button and click handler are suppressed; a disabled thumbnail's open and remove buttons stay focusable and announced as disabled, and call nothing.

A toast dismissed while it had no row on screen — hidden past `maxVisible`, or dismissed before it first rendered — now leaves the stack. Before, it stayed as an empty, invisible row that took a visible slot when it came back into view and kept the "Notifications" landmark (and its F6 stop) present after every real toast was gone.

Tokenizer: once a field has tokens, its text cursor sits right after the last token, on the last row, instead of at the end of the first row. PowerSearch gets the same fix. When the last row is too full for the cursor, focusing starts a new row for it; when it fits the cursor but not the typing area, the first keystroke moves to a new row. At rest the field keeps its height.

Internal: Tokenizer's touch sheet presentation is held back until its user experience is finished. The implementation stays in the package, reachable only through an internal entry reserved for Astryx's own packages; `TokenizerProps` offers no `experimental.presentation`, every Tokenizer renders the inline combobox, and nothing a consumer sees changes.

Tokenizer: tokens wrap before the clear-all button and busy indicator instead of running under them, including PowerSearch filters. While the field has tokens and can search, the busy indicator's space stays reserved, so a search starting or settling does not move token rows

`Tooltip`: an open tooltip that has moved clear of its trigger now also stays clear when the trigger moves on screen without resizing, in layout or because the page scrolled, at most one painted frame later. Moving it keeps every animation in its content where it was.

`Tooltip`: a tooltip taller than the room above and below its trigger no longer opens over the trigger. It opens beside the trigger when there is room there, otherwise on the other side if it fits there, and otherwise on the side with more room, sized to that room, scrolling content it cannot show. It also moves clear when its content grows, or its trigger or the viewport resizes, while it is open. Before, it slid over its own trigger, where a resting pointer could lose it, and content past the viewport could not be read. Tooltips that fit are placed exactly as before.

TopNav: with reduced motion on, the mega-menu panel no longer rises as it opens and closes. On a touch screen it fades, in 200 ms or less; with a mouse it opens and closes at once (design:reduced-motion).
A mouse slide across TopNavMenu's action items (items with an `onClick` and no `href`) no longer selects their text.

Internal: the touch motion tables register their springs, durations and curves as internal motion roles, each read once when a motion starts, so every component keeps its measured value. Nothing public changes: themes do not set motion roles, and no shipped component reads the roles yet.

`presentation="adaptive"` on DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, MoreMenu, Selector and MultiSelector, and a DropdownMenu's or ContextMenu's default sub-menu drill-in, now use the theme's compact definition with a coarse primary pointer: a viewport narrower than the theme's `md` point (768px by default) or shorter than 500px. This is a behavior change. The old default was a bottom sheet at 768px wide and below on a coarse pointer. Now a coarse-pointer screen exactly 768px wide keeps the anchored popover, and a phone in landscape (wider than 768px but shorter than 500px) gets the bottom sheet and the drilled-in sub-menu. A theme that moves `md` moves the edge with it. To pin a component's presentation regardless of the rule, pass `presentation="popover"` or `presentation="bottom-sheet"`; to keep a sub-menu's flyout, pass `presentation="flyout"` on `DropdownMenuSubMenu`. Mouse and keyboard users on desktop see no change, because every case requires a coarse pointer.

Adds an internal entry, reserved for Astryx's own packages, through which Lab components reach the gesture core that Core components import directly. No component uses it yet, and apps import nothing new.
