TreeList chevrons and hierarchy guides sit 4px closer to the row's inline start, and the chevron-to-label gap widens from 4px to 8px; labels keep their position.

Typeahead and Tokenizer hide the previous empty-result row while the next query debounces or waits for its answer. The existing input spinner provides loading feedback; no replacement Loading row is added. Settled empty results and their announcements remain unchanged. Fixes #8903.

Taps that start typing in a search field raise the touch keyboard. A tap on a Typeahead's selected value (edit mode) and a tap on the clear button of a Selector or MultiSelector search row now focus the input inside the tap itself instead of one frame later; iOS raises its keyboard only for a focus made while the browser is still handling the tap, so the deferred focus left a caret with no keyboard until a second tap. A clear tapped while the keyboard is already up keeps it up, as before. Introduced in #8158; final-state evidence (#8247).

BaseTypeahead, and the Typeahead, Tokenizer and PowerSearch menus built on it: an option now takes the highlight when the pointer moves over it, not when it merely appears under a resting pointer. A menu opened from the keyboard, or one that scrolls during arrow-key navigation, used to hand its highlight to whichever option slid under the cursor, so Enter could pick an option the user never pointed at and arrow keys appeared to jump back. The keyboard highlight now stays put until the pointer actually moves.

Internal: the UIKit constants table for touch presentations (springs, scroll physics, timing curves and navigation values), each value with its source and a checked list of the simulator measurements still owed. Not exported from the package entry point; no component reads it yet.

Internal: the UIKit gesture thresholds are one export per recognizer (`UIKIT_TAP`, `UIKIT_PAN`, `UIKIT_PRESS`, …), so a touch component bundles only the group it reads. The table's notes say that the status-bar scroll-to-top does not coast under Reduce Motion and that UIKit's Reduce Motion menu spring is never played. No behavior change.

Internal: the touch presentations' animator plays any closed-form curve (such as a spring chasing a moving target) through `play`, with the same presentation values, velocities, stop and shared clock as a spring, and the Reduce Motion policy. Not exported from the package entry point.

Internal: the touch presentations' animator follows design:reduced-motion (under Reduce Motion, an opacity-only cross-fade of 200 ms on a coarse pointer or after a touch release and an immediate change on any other pointer, with no option or theme value that keeps travel or lengthens the fade; an entrance or exit role orients a slide that changes no opacity), decided by its own planner module, and starts a call from rest when the browser commits it, as Core Animation does. Not exported from the package entry point.

Internal: a compositor animator for touch presentations. It plays UIKit's springs, and scroll coasts (built by a separate coast module, so a surface that never coasts does not carry them; `decay` plays momentum, and sends a spring back from past an edge through the Reduce Motion policy: a cross-fade on a coarse pointer or after a touch release, at once elsewhere) as Web Animations on translate, rotate, scale and opacity, so they keep running while JavaScript is busy, and reads values and velocities back from the curves for interruption, retargeting and Reduce Motion cross-fades. Not exported from the package entry point; no component uses it yet.

Internal: the spring, decay, rubber-band and projection math of UIKit for touch presentations, as pure functions checked against an independent integration and against values read from UIKit. Not exported from the package entry point; no component uses it yet.

`astryx upgrade` now reports stale generated files in a new `regenerate` receipt field, and reports code a codemod can identify but not migrate safely in the existing `declinedCandidates` list instead of failing. A manual migration is a `declinedCandidates` row with the file, its line as `location` when known, and a `reason` that starts with `manual migration needed (<codemod>):` followed by what to change (a file with several declined findings keeps one row listing each, with its own prefix, joined by `; `); it is printed after the run, does not fail the upgrade, and the run completes and exits 0. A generated file that must be rebuilt, such as stale theme CSS that `validate-data-token-ownership` reports and `astryx theme build` regenerates, is listed in `regenerate` with its rebuild command until it is rebuilt; a `hooks.postCodemod` command that rebuilds it clears it. When the project protects the file (for example an `@generated` header), the run is incomplete exactly as for a protected file (`complete: false`, `errorCode: "ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED"`, exit 1); when nothing protects it, it stays a codemod error (`ERR_CODEMOD_FAILED`, as before), now with the rebuild command in `regenerate`. Protected generated files also appear in `regenerate` with their header's `Command:`, and a reported file the project marks generated also appears in `protectedFiles` with the rule that protects it. A real codemod failure keeps its `ERR_CODEMOD_FAILED` error, and the `receipt` it carries lists both too.

A failed `astryx upgrade` now says which files it already changed. When a codemod or post-codemod hook fails, the upgrade still writes every other change; the `--json` error (`{"error", "code": "ERR_CODEMOD_FAILED"}`) now adds a `receipt` with the same fields a finished run returns (`modifiedFiles`, `errors`, `protectedFiles`, `complete: false`, `errorCode`), and the error `upgrade()` rejects with carries it as `receipt`. The change is additive: the error code, the error shape, `isError()`, the rejection and exit code 1 are unchanged. An error that stops the run after codemods have written files, such as an astryx.config that fails validation, carries a `receipt` too.

`useCombobox` (from `@astryxdesign/core/Selector`) now builds a combobox over a single-line text field you render yourself, such as a search field whose results replace a page section or an “add people” field in a dialog. Spread `getFieldProps` on your `input`, `getListboxProps` on your listbox wherever it renders, and `getOptionProps` on each option. Focus stays in the field; the field and the list carry the combobox roles and relationships; while the list shows, the arrows move the active option, Enter picks it and Escape hides the list without closing a surrounding dialog; while it is hidden, ArrowDown reopens it; while an input method is composing, keys reach the field untouched; a pointer picks without taking focus. Announce each new result count yourself through `useAnnounce`, with the words the field shows when nothing matches. Options may be any type with a string `value`. Existing options, return fields and `onKeyDown` behave as before.

VisuallyHidden keeps its clip block and its DOM clean: `xstyle`, `className` and `style` no longer reach the element. The component's contract is that content in the accessibility tree stays invisible, so its clip block is meant to be non-overridable — but the implementation spread leftover props onto the element, which wrote the literal attribute `xstyle="[object Object]"` into the DOM, and let the same props arriving through a cast or a `{...consumerProps}` object take the last word on `position` and un-hide the node while assistive technology kept announcing it.
changesets.body:
Measured prop by prop against `main`'s implementation, before and after this change:

- `xstyle` arrived as the attribute only — the `style` attribute stayed `null` and the clip classes were the same set in both arms — so a consumer passing it loses a stray attribute and no pixel.
- `className` was already displaced by the clip block's own class list; it reaches the element in neither arm.
- `style` did reach the element (`style="position: static;"`), and an inline declaration outranks a class rule, so the node was un-hidden. It stops reaching the element. That is the one rendering change here, and it moves the node back to the hidden state the contract calls non-overridable.

None of the three is styling surface on `VisuallyHiddenProps` — `className` and `style` are behind its `Omit`, reaching the element only through a cast or an untyped spread, and `xstyle` is documented as ignored — so no typed call site loses an effect it was promised.

`xstyle` stays declared on `VisuallyHiddenProps`, documented as ignored, because released 0.7.2 accepted it through `BaseProps`: removing it from the interface makes `<VisuallyHidden xstyle={…}>` stop compiling, and AST-017 FR31 and FR53 admit that narrowing only as a `[breaking]` change in a planned minor. It is deliberately not marked `@deprecated`: under FR28 a patch that deprecates a surface has to ship the exact migration or a codemod with it, and this fix ships neither. The removal and its migration belong to a planned minor, and the migration is to delete the prop — it applies nothing to the element.

changesets.headline: A two-finger pinch over an open picker wheel zooms the page again. The wheels in the TimeInput, DateTimeInput and DateInput bottom sheets accepted vertical pans only, which also refused the browser's pinch-zoom, so the page could not be zoomed over an open picker. They now leave the pinch to the page, as the menus and listboxes already do. Scrolling a wheel is unchanged.
